newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: REED-ELSEVIER STILL CONFIDENT ABOUT YR.
newsitem.headline: REED-ELSEVIER STILL CONFIDENT ABOUT YR.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch publishing group Reed-Elsevier said on Thursday it remained confident about the outlook for its full trading year.
The company was making the statement as part of a new procedure to issue a brief trading update towards the end of each fiscal year.

In August Reed Elsevier said it was confident about the business prospects for the second half of 1996, saying it would use strong cash flows to fund acquisitions and invest in its technological infrastructure.

Herman Bruggink and Nigel Stapleton, co-chairmen of Reed Elsevier said in a joint statement on Thursday: "Trading conditions in Reed Elsevier's main markets have been broadly unchanged since we announced our interim results in Augugst and we remain confident about the outlook for the year as a whole."
"Overall our businesses are maintaining the good organic growth trends demonstrated in the first half of the year," the chairmen's statement said.
They said that 1996 results, in contrast with 1995 which saw the full year benefit of the Lexis-Nexis acquisition, would include no significant impact from acquisitions.

Journal subscription renewal rates in scientific publishing have remained strong, while in legal publishing satisfactory first half trends have generally continued, the statement said. Strong first half revenue growth at Lexis-Nexis was being maintained, while margins were gradually improving.

The statement said the recent strengthening of the pound against the company's major trading currencies had in the second half reversed the two percent gain that currency translation had added to the growth in its first half attributable profit, leaving the full year impact broadly neutral.
In August Reed Elsevier announced headline first half 1996 pre-tax profit of 416 million stg, up from 370 million stg. In 1995 pre-tax profit before exceptional items was 723 million stg.
